feed.title: Hamon Lab
feed.subtitle: The Hamon Lab investigates how macrophage diversity shapes cancer progression, immune responses, and treatment outcomes. By combining human samples, spatial technologies, and experimental models, we aim to uncover new strategies to harness macrophage biology for cancer therapy.

entry.title: A new milestone for the lab!

link.title: A new milestone for the lab!

entry.content:
Congratulations to Camille Da Silva on being awarded a PhD fellowship!

After joining the Macrophages & Cancer team as a Master’s student, Camille will continue her research with us as our first PhD student.

Her PhD project will focus on understanding the role of macrophages in liver cancer, with a particular interest in how macrophage diversity and function influence tumor progression and response to therapy.

This fellowship marks an important milestone for Camille and for our young team. Congratulations again, Camille!

entry.title: New publication in Science: cDC1 orchestrate tertiary lymphoid structures in cancer

link.title: New publication in Science: cDC1 orchestrate tertiary lymphoid structures in cancer

entry.content:
We are pleased to share our new study published in Science, exploring how dendritic cells regulate tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) in cancer.

In this work, we show that mature cDC1 play a central role in the development and maintenance of TLS. By coordinating antigen presentation to both CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ T cells, these dendritic cells help sustain functional TLS and support effective anti-tumor immune responses.

The study also highlights the therapeutic potential of targeting cDC1 to strengthen TLS function and potentially improve responses to cancer immunotherapy.

This was a highly collaborative effort, and it was a pleasure to contribute to this work.

entry.title: FRM AJE funding for the Macrophages & Cancer team

link.title: FRM AJE funding for the Macrophages & Cancer team

entry.content:
We are grateful to the Fondation pour la Recherche Médicale (FRM) for supporting our research through its Amorçage de Jeunes Équipes (AJE) program.

This funding will support the development of our research program investigating the role of macrophages in liver cancer and their contribution to response and resistance to immunotherapy.

Our goal is to better understand the diversity and function of macrophages within the tumor microenvironment and ultimately identify new therapeutic strategies that could improve responses to cancer immunotherapy.

The FRM AJE funding will also contribute to the growth of the Macrophages & Cancer team and support the development of our experimental and translational research program.

We are very grateful to the FRM for their support and to all the mentors, collaborators, and colleagues who contributed to the development of this project.

entry.title: Young Investigator Masterclass CRC 2026
entry.content:
The Young Investigator Masterclass CRC 2026 brought together young investigators and mentors for two days of scientific exchange, mentoring, and career development at the Centre de Recherche des Cordeliers.

The program combined mentoring sessions, career discussions, scientific project challenges, networking activities, and one-to-one exchanges. Participants had the opportunity to discuss their projects, share experiences, and explore the many paths that a research career can take.

A particularly valuable part of the Masterclass was the openness of the discussions. Beyond scientific achievements, mentors shared their perspectives on the challenges, decisions, successes, and failures that have shaped their careers.

A huge thank you to all the mentors and participants for their enthusiasm and engagement, and to everyone who contributed to making these two days possible.

We look forward to seeing the collaborations, projects, and careers that will emerge from the conversations started during the Masterclass.
